News.title: Wage growth slumps to five-year low
News.content:
Workers are seeing the slowest pay rises in more than five years in a blow to households already facing soaring bills triggered by the war in Iran.

Average wages grew by 3.6pc in the three months to February, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS). This was the weakest rise since the quarter to November 2020.

Adjusting for inflation, British workers’ pay increased by only 0.2pc.

Slowing wages will raise the pressure on families, as the war in Iran pushes up the cost of living.

The ongoing conflict is expected to drive up food inflation to more than 9pc by the end of the year, according to forecasts by the Food and Drink Federation. Average households energy bills are expected to rise close to £2,000 a year, while petrol and diesel prices have already spiked.

Martin Beck, chief economist at WPI Strategy, said: “Weaker pay growth will compound the squeeze on households from higher energy prices and supply chain disruption linked to the conflict in the Middle East.

“While recent diplomatic developments may limit the worst-case outcomes, a period of falling real wages is still likely in the second half of the year, weighing on consumer spending and, in turn, labour demand.”

The public sector is better protected, with wages still growing by 5.2pc annually compared with a rise of 3.2pc in the private sector.

Unemployment surprisingly fell before the conflict, the ONS said, though it remains the hardest time since Covid to find a job with far more jobseekers than open roles.

The jobless rate fell to 4.9pc in December to February, down from 5.1pc in the previous three months.

Economists said the fall was mainly driven by rising economic inactivity, meaning they are no longer classified as unemployed, rather than more people finding work.

Modupe Adegbembo at Jefferies said: “This apparent improvement was entirely flattered by falling participation rather than stronger hiring. The decline in labour force participation mechanically reduced the unemployment rate, masking continued softness in actual labour demand.”

The number of employees on the nation’s payroll fell by 65,000 in the year to March.

Job losses have been concentrated among younger workers, with 242,000 fewer people under the age of 35 in work since since Rachel Reeves’s maiden Budget in October 2024, ONS figures show. By contrast, there are almost 100,000 more people aged 35 and older employed compared to October 2024.

There are now 2.5 unemployed people per vacancy, which makes it is the toughest time to find work since early 2021.

The number of advertised jobs fell to 711,000 in March, the lowest number in five years. Outside of the pandemic, vacancies are at an 11-year low.

Sports.title: The five dilemmas Man Utd chiefs face over Carrick including Solskjaer factor… and five reasons he should get the job
Sports.content:
THE CHAMPIONS League anthem is all but certain to be restored to the Old Trafford pre-match playlist next season.

That will largely be down to Michael Carrick’s impact since he was parachuted in at Manchester United in mid-January.





Eight wins from 12 games in a sub-standard Premier League season has elevated United to third and sixth-placed Chelsea have been all but cut adrift of the Champions League places.

Two years ago, United pointlessly held an end-of-season review to determine whether or not to sack Erik ten Hag.

After two weeks in which they drew conclusions which had long since been concluded, they lost their nerve and kept Ten Hag as United had won the FA Cup final.

Waiting until this season has concluded to make a decision on Carrick’s position is entirely sensible but United should not require an additional fortnight to make up their minds.



Their final five fixtures could have a bearing. United should be aiming to finish third and coming fourth or fifth would possibly feel anti-climactic.

But, come the final day at Brighton on May 24, there will be ample evidence for United to have decided on whether to stick or twist.

Here are the cases for and against…

The case for…

Results



Since Carrick’s first match in charge – the 2-0 triumph against Manchester City – United have entered the Champions League qualifying places and never dropped out of them.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Such stability has been unheard of at United in the past two-and-a-half years and they have regained a modicum of consistency under their former captain.

Carrick has a win percentage of 67 per cent and overseen victories against top six clubs City, Arsenal, Aston Villa and Chelsea, with potentially a fifth to in the offing against Liverpool next week.

The wins at Arsenal and Chelsea also ended eight-year and six-year droughts at those points of the London compass.



United’s performance level has not matched their results and they peaked in the January derby, their best display since the 2024 FA Cup final.

But results take precedence in the final stretch and United have responded to their two defeats under Carrick with wins.

Even on their worst night under him against Leeds, United were the better side for the final half-an-hour – with ten men.

Ahead of the curve



It is not beyond the realms of possibility that Manchester City, Arsenal, Liverpool, Chelsea and, or, Newcastle could change coaches in the summer.

For once, uncertainty mounts over the futures of coaches at United’s competitors and United could have a headstart if they keep Carrick.

Come United’s first pre-season friendly against Wrexham on July 18, Carrick would have been back in the building for six months, earned the respect of the players, improved performances, the league position and morale.

The 44-year-old knows what constitutes standards at United and he has assembled an exciting and energetic backroom staff by bringing in Steve Holland and Jonathan Woodgate, whilst retaining the popular Travis Binnion.



Carrick has held dialogue about recruitment and, as a garlanded midfielder, is uniquely placed to advise on how United should go about reinforcing their priority position.

No ideal elite external candidate available

The second favourite for the United job is Julian Nagelsmann, the Germany coach who has not managed in club football for three years.

Behind him are Andoni Iraola and Oliver Glasner, almost by default as their clubs have already announced they will be leaving in the summer. Then it is Gareth Southgate, more addicted to Linkedin than Liam Rosenior.



This is not like ten years ago, when United had a free run at free agent Jose Mourinho. In 2022, Mauricio Pochettino was going to become available and it cost only £2.5million to release Erik ten Hag from his Ajax contract.

Realistically, it would be an about-turn from United to make a beeline for Xabi Alonso. Xavi has not coached in two years and settling for an exotic name backfired with Ruben Amorim.

Eddie Howe, possibly on his way out at Newcastle, was of greater interest when Dan Ashworth and Sir Dave Brailsford were on the scene at United.

United’s aim is to mount a first genuine title challenge since they last won it next season. Carrick is guaranteed to finish above Premier League peers Iraola, Howe and Glasner, so there is logic in continuing with him.

Academy asset



Carrick has a vested interest in the United academy, given his son Jacey is in it, but his passion is genuine and dates back to his playing days at the club.

His presence at under 18 and under 21 games has given the academy added exposure and Carrick has already coached some members of the FA Youth Cup finalists.

Amorim was not as glowing about the academy’s starlets and most of his criticism was valid.

From the United power brokers’ perspective, having a coach who is invested in the academy ticks a box.



Compliance

Carrick does not rock the boat. Amorim almost caused it to capsize before he effectively engineered his own sacking in the new year.

Some at United would occasionally like Carrick to be more opinionated on particularly positive topics but it is admirable he won’t compromise his placid personality.

Carrick is a collegiate colleague whose press conferences are not cause for the United power brokers to peer through their fingers.



The case against…

Performances

By his own admission, Carrick was dissatisfied with the performance at Chelsea on Saturday.

Since United’s four-game winning streak at the start of Carrick’s tenure ended, their performance level has dipped. United’s most comfortable win – against ten-man Tottenham – required a goal in the final ten minutes to open up a two-goal lead.

Director of football Jason Wilcox’s scrutinising of a lifeless performance against Wolves led to Amorim’s sacking as he took exception to the constructive criticism.



United have not performed as soullessly under Carrick but they have not truly convinced for two months and they need to be confident that Carrick will arrest that.

Busier schedule

Carrick has capitalised on United’s sparse schedule of one game per week but they will have European football next season.

United have had two games under Carrick where they have played three days after their previous fixture and they have won neither of them. Those performances away at West Ham and Newcastle were among their worst.



Even though United’s squad consists of players accustomed to midweek matches, they have nestled into a curious comfort zone of mainly weekend-only games.

Ultimately, Carrick is unproven in juggling a domestic and European schedule, apart from his 11-day caretaker stint in November and December 2021

Better coaches are available

As good a job as Carrick has done, Iraola’s and Glasner’s track records suggest they are better coaches.



Iraola will have completed three seasons with Bournemouth and achieving finishes of 12th, ninth and maybe eighth would be a minor miracle at such a provincial club.

Glasner’s spell at Crystal Palace will total two-and-a-quarter years and he may have packed two trophies into the Eagles’ golden age.

Alonso has a managerial record that trounces Carrick’s, going off his Bundesliga success with Bayer Leverkusen. Perish the thought, but Enzo Maresca and Sean Dyche have achieved more on the touchline.

Some of those names are contrary but there is clear evidence that more experienced managers are on the market.



The Solskjaer factor

It was telling that while Kieran McKenna was attempting to secure a third promotion as Ipswich Town manager and Carrick was attempting to secure the United job at the weekend, Mike Phelan was coaching club legends in South Korea.

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s only job since United sacked him in November 2021 remains his seven-month spell at Besiktas.

It is pretty clear that the innovators from Solskjaer’s United regime were Carrick and McKenna, with Phelan a borderline redundant ‘assistant manager’.



Carrick is a modern coach, unlike Solskjaer, and his mid-season impact seems set to end with Champions League qualification, unlike Solskjaer in 2019.

But the parallels between the old colleagues and friends are still relevant. United got burnt when they upgraded Solskjaer from caretaker to permanent manager and his third and second-placed finishes came during the fake football of the Covid-19 pandemic.

Wilcox, now at United for two years, alarmingly considered rehiring Solskjaer in January. Going for the most in-house external choice could be a slippery slope.

Charisma question

This is a selfish and niche addition but an important one. A United manager usually has to ooze charisma and that is not Carrick’s natural personality.



When the chips were down for Sir Alex Ferguson, he tended to be on his best form in press conferences. Jose Mourinho was similar. Amorim was box office and Louis van Gaal’s wine-and-mince-pie walkout came in the midst of a winless December he somehow survived.

Ferguson said he played two matches a week and one was the press conference. Carrick does not have a game-face on for his weekly gatherings at Carrington and it has not done him any harm so far.

There will be bumps in the road, though, and it is in Carrick’s interests to have some goodwill banked to keep the vultures at bay.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ten Hag came unstuck on that front. Curiously, the Dutchman was a chipper and warm presence off camera but could be cold and gruff on it.



Had he showcased that true personality when the cameras were rolling, Ten Hag might still be in charge of United.

Sports.title: ‘Seriously unserious player’ – Fans can’t believe what Cherki was doing while huge Man City vs Arsenal brawl broke out
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY star Rayan Cherki has caused a stir on social media after fans noticed his latest stunt.

He was spotted doing keepy ups during a huge brawl between City and Arsenal players.





Cherki has built a reputation for being a wind-up merchant following his antics at Wembley after City beat Arsenal in the Carabao Cup final.

He goaded the Arsenal fans while appearing to pretend to be injured.

And fans took to X to react to his latest behaviour as he casually juggled the ball while City and Arsenal players clashed.



One fan posted: “Seriously unserious player.”

Another wrote: “Arsenal fans haven’t seen this footage, they’ll explode.”

While a third said: “Bro just wants to play football.”

City went on to win the huge match 2-1, putting them just three points behind Arsenal with a game in hand.



And Cherki was the star again as he danced through Arsenal’s backline and finished neatly to give his side the lead.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Following Kai Havertz‘s equaliser, top scorer Erling Haaland regained City’s advantage.

The post-match reaction also made headlines as BBC pundits Wayne Rooney and Danny Murphy criticised the City players’ celebrations – branding them “over the top”.

Gianluigi Donnarumma was spotted jumping in the crowd, while Erling Haaland cheekily side-eyed the camera and smirked.



Pep Guardiola has since hit back at the criticism, calling it “stupid“.

Mikel Arteta will be looking to use City’s celebrations as motivation during his side’s title run-in.

Guardiola’s team host Burnley on Wednesday night with a win sending them top of the tree.

LIAM ROSENIOR has sensationally torn into his Chelsea players after their 3-0 away loss to Brighton.

The Blues have now lost five Premier League games in a row and have failed to score in any of those defeats.



They sit seven points adrift of the Champions League places with just four games to play.



When questioned if this was the worst loss of their recent run, under-pressure Rosenior did not hold back.

He said: “By far, by far. That was unacceptable in every aspect of the game. Unacceptable in attitude.

“I keep coming out and defending the players – that’s indefensible.

“That performance tonight, the manner of the goals we conceded, the amount of duels that we lost, the lack of intensity in the team and yeah, something needs to change drastically right now.”

When asked why Chelsea find themselves in this difficult spot, Rosenior let all of his visible frustrations out.

He said: “Why? We need to look in the mirror. I need to look in the mirror. But I can’t keep coming out here and defending some of the things that we’re seeing.

“Manchester United, genuinely result wasn’t there but I felt we turned a corner.

They also failed to land a shot on target in a Premier League game for the first time since February 2025, which, coincidentally, was also in a 0-3 defeat against Brighton at the AMEX Stadium.

Rosenior only took over at Stamford Bridge earlier this year, but he made a promising start in the dugout with a string of wins.

He does still have an FA Cup semi-final to look forward to at the weekend, but even that might not save his skin come the summer.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Rosenior continued to dissect dismal performance at the Amex Stadium.

“You can speak about a lack of confidence, or results not going our way. That doesn’t represent anything that I want to see, and I won’t ever see it again.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola hits back at ‘stupid’ criticism after Wayne Rooney warned antics could come back to bite Man City
Sports.content:
PEP GUARDIOLA has hit back at the “stupid” criticism of Manchester City’s celebrations after beating Arsenal.

BBC pundits Wayne Rooney and Danny Murphy said the full-time whistle scenes at the Etihad on Sunday were “over the top”.





But boss Guardiola said: “People can say whatever stupid things they want — they celebrated because they knew if we didn’t win it would be ‘bye bye’ [for the title]. They won and still we are there. How can they not celebrate it?

“As much as you respect the opponent and their fans, celebrate however you want. We should wait until the end of the season to celebrate? Come on . . . ”

Gianluigi Donnarumma threw himself into the Etihad crowd and skipper Bernardo Silva whipped up fans following the 2-1 victory.

City could have more to toast tomorrow night as a win at Burnley would put them top. Guardiola tells his players to savour victories with fans -often joining them on a post-match walk around the pitch.



He added: “I said to them every game, ‘Go to our supporters’ and enjoy the moment.

“For us it was a final and, of course, you have to celebrate it.”

Pep reckons one reason they were so jubilant was because Arsenal are a “nightmare” to face.

He said: “Seeing how Arsenal play, I give them incredible credit. We had to sweat and fight to win because they have everything.”

Key midfielder Rodri looks set to miss the Clarets clash with a groin injury but the Spaniard is not expected to be out for long.

Meanwhile, Guardiola is tipping his ex-skipper Vincent Kompany to one day replace him at the Etihad.

The 40-year-old Belgian – in charge at Turf Moor the last time City visited almost three years ago – won a second straight Bundesliga title as Bayern Munich boss.



Guardiola said: “Sooner or later, I have a feeling he will decide it is time to come back to England. I’m sure Manchester’s in his heart.

“I said when we played Burnley, ‘He will be a manager here’.”

Sports.title: Brighton 3 Chelsea 0: Blues fans chant ‘f*** off Rosenior’ with manager on verge of sack after setting new horror record
Sports.content:
MARC Cucurella and his Chelsea team-mates should shave their heads in apology for this.

Cucurella and his barber had already let the Blues down by apparently leaking team news before kick off.





Then the Spaniard and the men in a funeral-black kit gave a display which could be the death of Liam Rosenior’s reign as head coach.

That was certainly the verdict of the away fans with more than a quarter of the game to go.

“F**k off, Rosenior,” they sang, as their team slumped towards a record-breaking fifth league defeat in a row without scoring.

The Brighton fans responded with chants of “Liam Rosenior, he’s one of our own” in slightly mocking honour of their former player and coach.



Sadly for him, the 41 year old will surely be a former Chelsea boss sooner rather than later.

It was disrespectful enough that the absence of injured pair Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro was broadcast on social media hours before kick off.

But the biggest kick in the teeth was how Rosenior’s team played.

Nevertheless, full credit to the Seagulls and head coach Fabian Hurzeler for taking advantage of the Blues’ weakness.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

How the home crowd enjoyed it.

Hurzeler’s side dominated and sometimes bullied a visiting team which had three former Brighton players in it, even without Pedro.

After Ferdi Kadioglu’s first-half goal andJack Hinshelwood killed the game with the second.

Substitute Danny Welbeck grabbed a late third so that the scoreline was closer to reflecting the home side’s true superiority.

Victory took the Seagulls above Chelsea and up to sixth in the table, right in the hunt for European football.



The Blues may miss out on continental competition entirely at this rate, which would be a disaster and, for Rosenior, impossible to survive.

The definition of madness, they say, is doing the same thing over and over again, and expecting a different result.

Rosenior had to try something new. Picking five defenders was not the most obvious way of ending a goal drought of more than four Premier League games, but the Blues boss’ options were limited.

Pedro and Palmer were the only Chelsea players to have scored in the league since the start of February.

The new formation was basically a good old-fashioned 4-4-2.



But it was the same old Chelsea, who gave a first-half performance for their manager which would be best described as sackable.

Inside three minutes Pascal Gross had tons of space down the Brighton right to send in a cross which Kaoru Mitoma met on the volley.

Unlike in the weekend game at Spurs, the Japanese winger’s shot was saved.

But Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez was beaten after the resulting corner. Jorrel Hato’s weak header fell for Kadioglu and Wes Fofana helped the ball past Sanchez.

The Blues’ keeper was in action again in the 15th minute, athletically tipping over a header by Jan Paul van Hecke from another Gross cross.



Hurzeler’s team could smell the fear and attacked like Seagulls divebombing tourists for their chips on the Pier.

After Georginio Rutter wasted a decent opening, Jack Hinshelwood should have made it 2-0.

Sanchez’s latest horrendous mistake passing out from the back gifted the ball to Baleba in the penalty area.

The midfielder squared it to Hinshelwood, but the shot did not have enough power and Trevoh Chalobah cleared off the line. Sanchez showed his appreciation to his defender and soon made another stop from a Rutter cross-shot.



The lucky escape galvanised Chelsea a little. They looked a little less nervous at the back and even won a corner at the other end.

But Brighton’s Van Hecke and Rutter made poor passes when in promising positions and the only fear for the home fans was their team would pay for not turning their domination into more goals.



Rosenior had to change something at the break ahead of the biggest half of his short Chelsea reign.

He chose to send on Alejandro Garnacho for Fofana, which meant Cucurella dropping back into his more accustomed full-back position in the usual 4-2-3-1 set-up

Garnacho soon teed up Romeo Lavia, who fired over the bar.

“We’ve had a shot,” sang the away supporters.

Their team was playing better, but Brighton continued to threaten.



Mitoma spun on a Gross pass only to drag his shot wide. Yankuba Minteh appealed for a penalty against Cucurella.

And then Hinshelwood made amends.

Minteh escaped being called for handball and hacked clear. Somehow Chelsea were two against two at the back, which became two versus one when Caicedo fell over and decided only to jog back..

Rutter charged on towards Chalobah then played in Hinshelwood, who swept the ball home first time.

Mitoma fired wide, then Kadioglu forced two more good saves from Sanchez, whose shot-stopping at least cannot be questioned.



The away fans meanwhile turned on Chelsea supremo Behdad Eghbali.

The co-owner missed the Manchester United defeat at the weekend, when he was abused by pre-match protesters and in the stadium.

This time he was around to hear again just how little the supporters think of him and the head coach appointed only in January.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Garnacho and substitute Marc Guiu at least had shots, but both went wide.

A Chelsea goal would have been little consolation to anyone, least of all Rosenior. Welbeck’s late third was just another nail in the coffin.

Sports.title: Leicester RELEGATED to League One 10 years after winning Premier League title – but could still get EFL lifeline
Sports.content:
LEICESTER CITY have been relegated to League One – less than ten years after winning the Premier League.

And the Foxes become just the fifth team in the Premier League era to suffer back-to-back drops from the top flight to the third tier.





But despite being seven points off 21st-placed Blackburn with two games left, Gary Rowett’s men could still theoretically get an EFL lifeline.



Leicester’s 1-0 defeat at Portsmouth on Saturday – their 18th defeat of the Championship season – left them needing to win all three of their remaining games and hope other results went their way.

However, the inept King Power side slumped at the first hurdle with a 2-2 draw at home to Hull.

And that means 23rd-placed Leicester – on 42 points from 44 games – had their inevitable relegation sealed as they now cannot catch Rovers.

The full-time whistle sparked more fury at the players and board from those fans still left in the stadium.



Remarkably, the squad with a £42million wage bill and 1770 Premier League appearances would still be in the relegation zone even without their six-point deduction for breaching financial rules.

However, there could still be a reprieve for the Foxes, who have one win in their last 18 league games.

West Brom were charged with an alleged breach of Profit & Sustainability Rules earlier in April and could be hit with a points deduction.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

However, the Baggies’ breach – which they deny – is not thought to be as significant as Leicester’s and therefore a minimal points deduction is expected, which would dash the Foxes’ slim hopes.

West Brom easily beat Watford this evening and now sit ten points clear of Leicester with two games to go.



At the King Power, goalkeeper Asmir Begovic’s awful pass was emphatically punished by Liam Millar, who swept in on 18 minutes in front of swathes of empty blue seats before Patson Daka somehow misfired wide from close range.

Leicester showed uncharacteristic fight to turn the game around as Jordan James equalised from the spot – Leicester had missed their last three penalties – on 52 minutes before Luke Thomas put the hosts in front less than two minutes later on the volley.

The mood turned sour again shortly afterwards, though, when Rowett put villain Harry Winks on for fan-favourite James.

Winks’ arrival was greeted with a chorus of furious boos and X-rated chants following his angry altercation with a fan at Fratton Park.

Moments later, Oli McBurnie blasted past Begovic for 2-2 to hammer the final nail into Leicester’s Championship coffin as Daka hit the woodwork and Aaron Ramsey blazed over late on as it finished level and the unthinkable nightmare became a brutal reality.



The Foxes’ relegation is a staggering, pathetic and embarrassing fall from grace.

On May 2, 2016, their fairytale 5,000-1 Premier League title was confirmed as Eden Hazard’s goal sparked the famous Jamie Vardy party.



In 2017, they reached the Champions League quarter-finals.

In 2021, they won the FA Cup.

In 2022, they made the Conference League semi-finals.



Now they have plunged to three relegations in four seasons and join Swindon Town, Wolves, Sunderland and Luton Town in the unwanted group of teams to go from Premier League through to League One successively.

And the 2026-27 campaign will be just Leicester’s second season in the third tier in their 142-year history.

Their only previous year in League One came in 2008-09, when Nigel Pearson’s side romped to a record-breaking 96 points and 27 wins.

Not even the most optimistic Leicester fan can expect anything remotely similar at the King Power next season.

The club is rotten from top to bottom with overpaid players failing to perform, financial mismanagement, a deeply unpopular hierarchy and a bitterly divided fanbase.

Sports.title: Chelsea fans' X-rated Liam Rosenior message during embarrassing Brighton defeat
Sports.content:
Chelsea fans' X-rated Liam Rosenior message during embarrassing Brighton defeat

Chelsea slumped to a 3-0 defeat at Brighton as fan unrest grew, with the Blues now losing five consecutive Premier League matches under Liam Rosenior

View 2 Images Liam Rosenior was the target of some unsavoury chants by fans (Image: Darren Walsh, Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Travelling Chelsea supporters directed X-rated chants at manager Liam Rosenior as the Blues slumped to yet another dreadful defeat. The Seagulls secured a fourth straight victory over the west Londoners, cruising to a comfortable 3-0 home win.

‌



For Rosenior, it represented a fifth successive Premier League defeat and a seventh in eight matches across all competitions. It was a dismal performance from the very first whistle, as Ferdi Kadioglu capitalised on more woeful set-piece defending from the west Londoners to net after just three minutes.

‌



Rosenior abandoned the back-three system he had deployed from the outset and Chelsea initially appeared to have improved after the break, but Jack Hinshelwood extinguished any optimism by doubling the lead in the 56th minute. Deep into injury time, Danny Welbeck compounded the Blues' misery by adding a third.

‌



Between Brighton's second and third goals, chants of 'F*** off Rosenior' rang out from the travelling Chelsea faithful. Seagulls supporters then united in chants of 'Liam Rosenior, he's one of our own' in tribute to their former player.

The reaction from his former supporters will have done precious little to alleviate the mounting pressure on the Chelsea boss. A victory for the west Londoners would have significantly boosted their hopes of securing a Champions League berth. Should results continue to turn against them, Chelsea could soon find themselves as low as 11th.

Furious Liam Rosenior points the blame at Chelsea stars as fans turn on manager READ MORE :

Chelsea team news leaked by Marc Cucurella's BARBER hours before Brighton clash READ MORE :

The defeat left the Blues in seventh position on 48 points, now just two points above 11th-placed Sunderland and three ahead of Fulham, both of whom hold a game-in-hand over Chelsea.

‌



Following the final whistle, Rosenior made his way over to the travelling supporters and placed his hand on his chest in an apologetic gesture towards the Chelsea faithful. When pressed on whether this was his side's worst showing during the recent run of fixtures, Rosenior said: "By far. That was unacceptable in every aspect of the game, unacceptable in the attitude.

"I keep coming out to defend the players but that was indefensible tonight. Something needs to change drastically right now.

View 2 Images Chelsea were outclassed by Brighton (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"That performance tonight, the manner of the goals we conceded, the amount of duels that we lost, the lack of intensity in the team, something needs to change drastically.

"We need to look in the mirror. I need to look in the mirror. But I can't keep coming out here and defending some of the things that we're seeing."

‌



He further described it as a massive backward step following a relatively encouraging showing in the 1-0 home defeat to Manchester United at the weekend. Rosenior said: "Manchester United, genuinely result wasn't there but I felt we turned a corner.

"But the general attitude, spirit was lacking - determination from three or four of the starting eleven. That's nowhere near enough for this club. I can't come out and lie. I tell the truth. That was an unacceptable performance at every level."

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford failed 'golden chance' to secure Barcelona transfer as new details emerge
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford failed 'golden chance' to secure Barcelona transfer as new details emerge

Barcelona have an opportunity to offer Marcus Rashford a permanent contract this summer, but the Manchester Untied star's transfer saga has just taken a fresh twist

View 2 Images Barcelona could sign Marcus Rashford this summer (Image: Aitor Alcalde Colomer, Getty Images)

Marcus Rashford is said to have wasted a golden opportunity to establish himself with Barcelona this month and seal a permanent switch to the Camp Nou. The 28-year-old is currently on a season-long loan with the Catalan giants after burning bridges at Old Trafford.

‌



The England international fell out of favour under Ruben Amorim's management, spending the closing stages of last season on loan at Aston Villa before joining Barca in the summer on a 12-month deal. The La Liga leaders, however, possess an option to convert his stay into a permanent transfer at the end of the current campaign for approximately £26million.

‌



Rashford was presented with the chance to make that option an obvious decision this month when Raphinha sustained a hamstring injury. Yet the forward failed to truly seize it.

‌



Man Utd transfer already in danger as arch-rivals look to block Real Madrid swap READ MORE :

Rashford was given carte blanche to make an impression during Barcelona's Champions League quarter-final ties against Atletico Madrid this month - deployed as a starter in the opening encounter at the Nou Camp. Following a lacklustre display, he was demoted to the substitutes' bench for the return leg at the Metropolitano - with Dani Olmo stepping in instead.

As Barcelona ultimately exited the competition 3-2 on aggregate, it remains unclear whether Rashford will be afforded another opportunity to demonstrate his value in this weekend's La Liga fixture away at Getafe.

Meanwhile, Marca report that another complication may be emerging regarding a permanent switch to sunny Spain for Rashford this summer - namely that the club may be reluctant to meet United's asking price in one lumper.

‌



The publication claim that the club have floated the possibility of settling the clause through instalments. However, United's position is that they will not renegotiate their original agreement.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Barca sources reportedly indicated just months ago that satisfying Rashford's personal demands would not pose a problem, however, it is now suggested that the club are exploring alternative options to strengthen their forward line.

‌



With Robert Lewandowski's future at the club beyond 2025/26 uncertain, Barcelona could opt to instead deploy their resources by recruiting another natural striker rather than investing heavily in Rashford - who prefers the left flank.

The likes of Victor Osimhen and Dusan Vlahovic have each been touted with a switch to the Nou Camp recently - their respective salaries cutting into Barca's transfer budget should a deal for either materialise.

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford's Barcelona future is in doubt (Image: AP)

Article continues below

Should Rashford return to Greater Manchester, there's always a possibility that he could force his way back into first-team contention, given Amorim is no longer at the club and Michael Carrick recently left the door ajar to that prospect.

Speaking about Rashford's circumstances this month, he said: "There's decisions to be made on certain things, and obviously Marcus is in that situation. But at this point in time, nothing's been decided. It will be, because it has to be at a certain point, but at this stage, there's nothing to say."

However, with Carrick's own future at the club beyond the current campaign hanging in the balance - given he is only in an interim role with no assurance of being appointed permanently - Rashford cannot bank everything on one outcome.

Sports.title: Furious Liam Rosenior points the blame at Chelsea stars as fans turn on manager
Sports.content:
Furious Liam Rosenior points the blame at Chelsea stars as fans turn on manager

Chelsea boss Liam Rosenior's position was already coming under scrutiny prior to Tuesday night's damaging 3-0 loss against Brighton and he pulled no punches in a frank post-match interview

View 2 Images Liam Rosenior was furious after Chelsea's 3-0 loss at Brighton (Image: Sky Sports)

An irate Liam Rosenior tore into his team after Chelsea slumped to a chastening 3-0 defeat away at Brighton, branding their performance as "unacceptable" and "indefensible".

‌



The Blues were comprehensively beaten on the south coast courtesy of goals from Ferdi Kadioglu, Jack Hinshelwood and Danny Welbeck. A fifth straight defeat has only increased the scrutiny on Rosenior, with Chelsea losing five league matches in a row without scoring for the first time since 1912.

‌



Angry fans turned on Rosenior during the game and the former Strasbourg chief pulled no punches in a scathing post-match interview with Sky Sports.

‌



When asked if that was the worst performance of their poor run of form, Rosenior replied: "By far. That was unacceptable in every aspect. Unacceptable in terms of the attitude. I keep coming out and defending the players [but] that performance tonight was indefensible. Something needs to change drastically here right now.

OPINION John Cross Liam Rosenior fighting for his future as gutless Chelsea embarrassed by Brighton

Chelsea team news leaked by Marc Cucurella's BARBER hours before Brighton clash READ MORE :

When he was asked why he felt the players were so poor, Rosenior added: " We need to look in the mirror. I need to look in the mirror. I can't keep coming out here [and] defending some of the things that we're seeing.

‌



"At Manchester United, genuinely the result wasn't there, [but] I felt we'd turned a corner. But the general attitude [and] spirit was lacking [tonight]. Maybe three or four out of the 11 [performed] - that's nowhere near enough for this club. That's nowhere near enough. I can't come out and lie, I'll tell the truth. That was an unacceptable performance in every area."

Rosenior was handed a six-year contract by the Stamford Bridge hierarchy when he was appointed as Enzo Maresca's successor back at the start of January.

View 2 Images Chelsea were easily beaten by Brighton, who leapfrog them in the Premier League table (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

‌



But with the Blues now seven points off fifth-placed Liverpool and facing an uphill battle to qualify for the Champions League, pressure on the 41-year-old is likely to increase in the coming weeks.

He continued: "It's a really, really difficult night. The most difficult night, not even [just] here at this magnificent football club, but in my career. Some of the things I was witnessing today, I never want to see ever again.

"To be even accused of throwing the towel in, it's unacceptable. That's all I'm gonna say. I'm hurting. That doesn't represent me. That doesn't represent the football club in any way and that has to change, starting with the FA Cup semi-final on Sunday."

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola bites back at Wayne Rooney over 'stupid' Arsenal celebrations verdict
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola bites back at Wayne Rooney over 'stupid' Arsenal celebrations verdict

Wayne Rooney has been speaking about Manchester City's celebrations after beating Arsenal in a huge match at the weekend with games running out in the title race

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola has had his say after Wayne Rooney branded Manchester City's post-Arsenal celebrations 'over the top' (Image: Hayters TV)

Pep Guardiola has bit back at Wayne Rooney after he labelled Manchester City's celebrations 'premature' and 'over the top' following their huge win over Arsenal.

‌



City headed into Sunday's seismic encounter at The Etihad knowing that only a win would do with Arsenal six points ahead of them. And Guardiola's men managed to do just that with goals from Rayan Cherki and Erling Haaland earning them a priceless 2-1 victory to propel them back into within touching distance of Arsenal.

‌



With City having a game in hand on their title rivals, they could now overtake the Gunners on goal difference with a win away at Burnley on Wednesday night.

‌



Rooney brought up City's celebrations after the game with Gianluigi Donnarumma seen jumping into the crowd at the final whistle, pointing out that there were still plenty of games left in the title race.

Arsene Wenger issues new Premier League title prediction after Arsenal stumble READ MORE :

But Guardiola says people can say "whatever stupid things they like" and that Manchester City's celebrations were completely justified given the quality of their opponents and the magnitude of the game.

"When I’m on the sidelines and seeing how Arsenal is playing, I give give incredible credit. They are a top team, a contender to win the Champions League and top of the Premier League. I see that game and we had to sweat and fight to beat them because they have everything. So so competitive, their mentality and many, many things that they do well. They play short, they play well," he said.

‌



"They play long ball, they win the second ball. Set-pieces. It’s a nightmare. I give a lot of credit to compete with them and against them and the last two times beat them. I give a lot of credit to these players, they know it and feel it."

View 2 Images Gianluigi Donnarumma was in the thick of the celebrations after the game (Image: Getty Images)

Referencing Rooney's comments, he continued: "People can say whatever stupid things they want to say - they celebrated because they know the value of the opponent. They knew if we didn’t win it would be ‘bye bye’. They won and still we are there. How can they not celebrate it?

‌



"As much as you respect the opponent and the fans of the opponent, celebrate however you want. Wait until the end of the season to celebrate? Come on. I said to them ‘every single game go to our fans’ and enjoy the moment. What sense is not to live it? You have to celebrate just once if you win? And if you don’t win you cry all the time? Come on.

"Of course we are not going to celebrate it in the middle of the week if we win 3-0 or 4-0 and the opponent are different. Everybody knew that game. It was a final. Especially for us. Maybe not for them but for us it was a final and of course you have to celebrate it."

Sports.title: Hugo Ekitike sends defiant message as Liverpool star leaves hospital following Achilles injury
Sports.content:
Hugo Ekitike sends defiant message as Liverpool star leaves hospital following Achilles injury

Hugo Ekitike has shared an emotional social media post following his Achilles injury, with the Liverpool striker facing up to nine months on the sidelines

View 2 Images Hugo Ekitike ruptured his Achilles tendon (Image: Xavier Laine, Getty Images)

Hugo Ekitike posted: "I'm out of here, I'll be back soon," as he shared a poignant social media message following surgery. The Liverpool forward faces up to nine months on the sidelines after rupturing his Achilles tendon last week.

‌



The Frenchman collapsed during Liverpool's 2-0 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain at Anfield before being carried off on a stretcher. Arne Slot confirmed the devastating news afterwards, revealing that Ekitike faces an extended spell away from football while rehabilitating from the injury.

‌



And now, Ekitike has suggested he will be stepping back from social media as he continues his recovery. The 23-year-old posted an emotional series of images to Instagram on Tuesday afternoon from his @heesheki account, which has 431,000 followers.

‌



Liverpool learn impossible Mohamed Salah transfer verdict as Arne Slot gives update READ MORE :

The opening image showed him seated in a room wearing a protective boot on his leg, while an AI-generated clip portrayed him running off crutches and netting a goal against Manchester City.

Another showed Ekitike sitting in a wheelchair at hospital, while the fourth captured him gaming with friends.

Arguably the most heartbreaking was another AI-generated image of Ekitike standing in tears while wearing his France strip, reaching towards a shattered World Cup trophy.

‌



That references the reality that the striker will miss this summer's tournament in North America, as well as half of next campaign if projections prove accurate.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Ekitike also posted a brief video clip featuring the late rapper Mac Miller. The musician, who tragically passed away aged just 26 in 2018, can be heard saying in the footage: "Life is good though.

‌



"I want y'all to see that life is great. Your life is great too. Have a good time, man.

"Have some fun, having fun is okay. Get some love in your life, whether that be another person or just loving yourself, man. Love is good, spread love.

"Spread love. I'm out of here, I'll be back soon."

‌



View 2 Images Hugo Ekitike shared an emotional social media post (Image: Hugo Ekitike / Instagram)

Ekitike also shared the clip to his stories section on his account. Liverpool were swift to respond to the post, rallying behind their striker as he faces a lengthy road to recovery.

They wrote: "We're with you all the way, Hugo."

Article continues below

The Reds' next fixture is a home tie against Crystal Palace on Saturday, April 25.

For that match, they may be forced to call upon Alexander Isak to lead the attack, despite the Swede having only recently returned from a leg fracture he suffered back in December.

Sports.title: How Leicester City have gone from Premier League champions to League One in 10 years
Sports.content:
How Leicester City have gone from Premier League champions to League One in 10 years

Leicester City have been relegated to League One just a decade after lifting the Premier League trophy but signs of the Foxes’ demise have long been clear to supporters

View 4 Images Leicester have been relegated to League One (Image: Getty Images)

"If you think Leicester can be in League One, then you have lost your mind." They were the words of midfielder Jordan James in December when asked if Leicester City could be relegated once again.

‌



And to a certain extent, you can see where the Welsh midfielder was coming from. This is a club that only 10 years ago lifted the Premier League title under Claudio Ranieri.

‌



This is a club that only five years ago claimed the FA Cup for the first time in their history under the stewardship of Brendan Rodgers. This is a club that had allowed others to dream.

‌



That dream has very quickly transformed into a nightmare, having slipped into League One after a dismal campaign with a draw against Hull City officially confirming their fate. Leicester are now a warning of how not to run a competent football club.

Alarm bells ring

Alarm bells have actually been ringing since 2020 when the Midlands side suffered a late-season collapse and failed to secure a Champions League spot and the riches that came with it.

That drop in revenue, coupled with the Covid pandemic, hit the Foxes' Thai owners hard. Leicester then fell at the final hurdle again the following season but remained staunchly behind Rodgers.

‌



Frank Lampard scoops major EFL award after stunning Coventry City promotion READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

That glorious day under the Wembley arch against Chelsea followed and will stick long in the memory. But the abject failure of the club since then will arguably be remembered more vividly.

A disastrous 2021 summer transfer window saw the club waste huge funds on Patson Daka, Boubakary Soumare and Jannik Vestergaard - all without selling a key player to offset that splurge. Leicester are still paying the financial penalty of that business to this day.

‌



A 4-1 defeat to local rivals Nottingham Forest in the FA Cup as holders in February 2022 sticks out as a clear moment where the foundations of the King Power ownership began to crumble. Rodgers went on the defence and warned that the squad needed a ‘refresh’, while he also claimed that Leicester were 'not the same club' just months later.

The exits of title heroes Wes Morgan, Christian Fuchs and Kasper Schmeichel led to a shocking slip in standards, a symptom that has only worsened. The Foxes inevitably fell out of the Premier League the following season, with Rodgers sacked towards the end of that campaign in favour of Dean Smith - a decision that arguably came too late. Relegations happen, of course, but not to a squad as talented as Leicester’s was.

View 4 Images Leicester's downward trajectory started as far back as 2022 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Mistakes repeated

There should have been an inquest into how the club found themselves in such a position, particularly from one of such strength. One was certainly promised by the club ownership, with owner Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha confirming an ‘internal review’ which never materialised.

All club chiefs, including much-maligned director of football Jon Rudkin, retained their roles as if nothing ever happened. Leicester should have learnt their lesson. They simply did not.

‌



There was, however, a brief moment of solace during the 2023/24 campaign as the Foxes earned an instant return to the Premier League under Enzo Maresca. Even that successful campaign has now been tainted and ended up doing serious damage to Leicester in the long run.

The club splashed the cash in an effort to earn promotion, signing England internationals Harry Winks, Conor Coady and more on hugely inflated contracts for significant funds of around £18m.

Points deduction

That saw Leicester breach the EFL’s PSR rules once again. While they had successfully navigated previous charges on a technicality following relegation, they weren’t to have a lucky escape again (but more on that later).

‌



View 4 Images Enzo Maresca led Leicester back into the Premier League in 2024 (Image: Getty Images)

Leicester continued making the same dire mistakes upon their return to the top flight. Maresca left for Chelsea, with former Forest boss Steve Cooper appointed as his replacement. He was the wrong man from the start - some players making their affection for former boss Maresca clear in a Copenhagen nightclub shortly after his arrival.

The signings of Oliver Skipp, Jordan Ayew, Bobby De Cordova-Reid and Caleb Okoli also did little to inspire confidence that this was a squad equipped to stay up.

‌



Cooper was eventually sacked in November to be replaced by Ruud van Nistelrooy. The Dutchman’s spell at the helm could not have gone much worse, having lost 18 of his 25 Premier League games, ending in relegation. It proved that Leicester's demotion two seasons previously was not just a blip but a sign of a bigger issue.

Boardroom delays

It was also abundantly clear that the former Manchester United forward did not have a future at the King Power Stadium but it took until June 27 - over four weeks after the final game of the season - for Van Nistelrooy to be officially relieved of his duties. Another three weeks passed before his replacement Marti Cifuentes was appointed - just 26 days before the season opener - a delay that significantly hampered the club's pre-season preparations, as did the departure of the legendary Jamie Vardy without a proper replacement being signed.

Away from a positive start, Cifuentes proved to be another dismal appointment, amassing just 10 league wins before being sacked in January. It then took Leicester almost a month to find his replacement in Gary Rowett.

‌



View 4 Images Gary Rowett has failed to drag Leicester away from relegation (Image: Getty Images)

In that time, Leicester lost three consecutive games including a 4-3 reverse at the hands of Southampton where they let a three-goal lead slip. That defeat appears to have done irreparable damage to the dressing room, as did a six-point deduction for their previous PSR breaches, the first time ever that the club had seen points taken off them. An appeal was thrown out by an independent commission, landing Leicester in a relegation battle.

Anyone thinking that off-pitch governance is the main reason behind their slip into the third tier is woefully mistaken, though. Rowett has fared the same as many of his predecessors by failing to get a tune out of an expensively-assembled squad who appear unfazed by the plight that the club finds themselves in.

‌



The former Millwall boss has just one win to his name - a run of form that has seen Leicester drop into League One for just the second time in their history. Even without their points deduction, Leicester would still be in the relegation zone and under real threat of a place in the third tier.

Given the trajectory that the club has long been on, anyone that thinks Leicester don’t deserve to be in League One have lost their mind.

Sports.title: Liam Rosenior fighting for his future as gutless Chelsea embarrassed by Brighton
Sports.content:
Liam Rosenior fighting for his future as gutless Chelsea embarrassed by Brighton

BRIGHTON 3-0 CHELSEA: Liam Rosenior's side lost for the fifth straight time in the Premier League - failing to score in the process - with pressure piling on the manager

View 3 Images Chelsea manager Liam Rosenior looks on during the defeat to Brighton

There is a tipping point in every manager’s reign. And just three months into his time at Chelsea, it feels like Liam Rosenior will do well to survive after this.

‌



This was humiliating, gutless and when the fans turn in such brutal fashion then there is often no way back. The traveling Chelsea fans were chanting “f*** off Rosenior” as they also made their feelings plain towards co-owner Behdad Eghbali who was sat up in the stands.

‌



This is a club which feels like it has lost its soul and is in serious danger of imploding without Champions League football next season which already looks beyond them.

‌



Incredibly, this was the first time Chelsea have lost five league games in a row without scoring a goal since 1912. That was the year the Titanic sunk - and Chelsea are going down just as fast.

The Chelsea soap opera always provides a story and this time Marc Cucurella’s barber leaked the team news on social media that Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer were out injured.

Chelsea team news leaked by Marc Cucurella's BARBER hours before Brighton clash READ MORE :

But even a mix-and-match Chelsea team should show more pride than this. It was downright embarrassing and sadly reflects badly on the manager because the players did not show much fight.

‌



They were run ragged by Brighton and the only relief was that Fabian Hurzeler’s side did not score more goals which would have only increased the pressure on Rosenior.

The home fans were even chanting Rosenior’s name themselves as he used to play for Brighton and that just rubbed salt in the wounds.

Chelsea’s season is drifting towards chaos and, even with four games left, the owners are left with a tough decision.

‌



You have to feel some sympathy for Rosenior because he is a good young coach, an honourable person and could not have turned the job down.

View 3 Images Ferdi Kadioglu scored the opener for Brighton against Chelsea

But it has left him exposed in trying to run a basket case of a club who have spent more than £1billion on the team - and it still looks a complete mess.

‌



Brighton were ahead inside three minutes. Man of the match Pascal Gross sent over and corner, it was flicked on and there was Ferdi Kadioglu to drove home his first goal in 17 months.

Chelsea keeper Robert Sanchez kept his team in it. But he made yet another error as his pass went straight to Carlos Baleba who laid it off to Jack Hinshelwood who seemed certain to score but fit-again Trevoh Chalobah made a heroic last ditch clearance.

Rosenior had switched to a back three - only the second time in his reign - but he abandoned that at half time as Alejandro Garnacho came on for Wesley Fofana. But they looked vulnerable in defence and toothless in attack.

‌



But for all of Brighton’s superiority, they had to wait for a second. It came after 56 minutes. Chelsea appealed in vain when the ball hit Yankuba Minteh’s arm but referee Craig Pawson waved it away.

View 3 Images Brighton move into sixth after beating Chelsea

Georginio Rutter led the charge, he laid the ball off for Hinshelwood and the Brighton midfielder swept home to make the result safe.

‌



The Chelsea fans grew even more frustrated as their chants off “f*** off Rosenior got even louder as the night wore on and the crisis engulfing the club deepened.

Finally Brighton got a third which was no more than they deserved as supersub Danny Welbeck steered in from close range.

Rosenior appears to be out of his depth and Chelsea’s experiment - gambling on a rookie manager in charge of a team which was crowned world champions last year - looks to be backfiring.

Sports.title: Coventry City crowned Championship champions after sealing Premier League return
Sports.content:
Coventry City crowned Championship champions after sealing Premier League return

Coventry City have already ended their near 30-year exile from the Premier League and Frank Lampard’s men have now rounded off their season by securing the Championship title

View 2 Images Frank Lampard has guided Coventry City to the Championship title

Coventry City have added the Championship title to their promotion to the Premier League. The Sky Blues sealed their return to the top flight last week with a 1-1 draw against Blackburn.

‌



And their 5-1 win against Portsmouth at the CBS Arena on Tuesday evening has seen them rubber-stamp the trophy with two games remaining.

‌



The title rounds off a stunning season for the Midlands side, with Frank Lampard’s men having led the way in the Championship for the majority of the campaign. Coventry take on Wrexham and Watford in their final two games of the campaign and could end the campaign on 95 points.

‌



That haul has seen boss Lampard crowned as the EFL Championship Manager of the Season. Speaking at Sunday’s awards ceremony, the Chelsea icon said: "I was emotional the other night [securing promotion at Blackburn] because it dawned on me in that moment what we had achieved.

Harry Redknapp recalls Frank Lampard leaving son Jamie needing 24 stitches after brutal clash READ MORE :

Frank Lampard makes Coventry transfer plea after sealing Premier League return READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"A club that I walked into 16 months ago that had gone to the depths and back up, and football is always about people and always about supporters and I'd missed it.

‌



"You have to credit Mark Robins [previous head coach] for what he did at the club, the owner Doug King and appreciate the moment, and I'm working with a great group of players.

"When you walk into a group forget the football talent, that's obviously important but when they look after themselves, they train well, they support each other, they have a laugh, that's the gold. It's an incredible story and I'm pleased to be a part of it."

Asked about the prospect of playing Premier League football, Lampard said: "There's a lot of work to do because we know the step that it will be for the football club.

‌



View 2 Images Haji Wright scored the opener for Coventry as they clinched the title in emphatic fashion

"So that's something we have to work on quickly now because of where we're at, we have to be ambitious -- we're Coventry City football club.

"I know what the Premier League is and its going to be a challenge, we can enjoy the moment for the next two weeks, but of course we have to work behind the scenes to ensure we go up the right way."

Article continues below

With Coventry being confirmed as champions, it leaves a clutch of clubs battling it out for the second automatic promotion spot. Ipswich, Millwall, Southampton and Middlesbrough all remain in contention heading into the final two matchdays of the campaign.
